# OA v0.7.28

**Status:** Public development preview

**Release date:** 2026-08-30

**Source:** [`v0.7.28`](https://github.com/realminc/oa/releases/tag/v0.7.28)

## Summary

OA v0.7.28 publishes the completed CPU-only Vulkan Linear Math foundation used
by OA rendering, camera, scene, animation, rigging, and SDK simulation paths.
It replaces the immutable `v0.7.27` candidate, which was blocked before build
by the hosted generator-policy gate. The repair changes only the spelling of
one namespace declaration; VLM behavior and measurements are unchanged.

## Added

- Packed `Mat3`/`DMat3`, affine construction and decomposition, checked normal
  matrices and inverses, signed scale, shear, and reflection handling.
- All six named Euler orders, robust quaternion conversion and interpolation,
  checked from-to/look rotation, and stable axis/angle queries.
- Fixed-convention right-handed Vulkan camera and projection math, including
  finite/infinite reversed-Z and top-origin viewport project/unproject.
- A paired OA/GLM benchmark covering 50 operation families in `F32` and `F64`,
  with a correctness oracle before every timed case.

## Improved

- Specialized fixed-shape `Mat4` multiplication, TRS construction, determinant,
  normalization, quaternion, interpolation, inverse, and look-at paths while
  preserving packed ABI and conditioned fallbacks.
- Migrated Render camera, mesh, scene and renderer code plus SDK transform and
  skeleton consumers to named VLM authority.
- Kept public VLM values independent of xsimd while permitting compiler-native
  vectorization of visible fixed-shape formulas.

## Fixed

- Split the compressed `oa::FnScene` namespace declaration into the explicit
  nested blocks required by OA's operation-schema drift checker.

## Performance

On the qualified Intel Core i5-1145G7 / Clang 22.1.8 Release host, all 27
equivalent valid-input arithmetic families reached parity or lower time than
GLM 1.1.0 in both precisions. Geometric-mean time was 13.4% lower for `F32` and
11.9% lower for `F64`. `F32` `Mat4` multiplication used 37.8% less time; TRS
composition used 64.2% less `F32` time and 67.8% less `F64` time.

These are workload- and host-specific results, not a universal fastest-library
claim. Checked operations are reported separately from raw GLM operations.
See the complete [VLM benchmark](../benchmarks/oaVlm.md).

| Schema coverage and drift | Pass: 316/316 contracts, 246/246 Python exposure; public namespace policy clean |
| VLM contract/property suite | Pass: 39/39 tests |
| Focused Release consumers | Pass: VLM, Camera, Scene, Transform, Skeleton |
| ASAN/LSAN | Pass: focused closure; no sanitizer finding |
| UBSAN | Pass: focused closure; no sanitizer finding |
| OA/GLM oracle | Pass: all 100 precision/case pairs |

The public tagged workflow owns the complete hosted build, sanitizer, package,
wheel, release-asset, checksum, and PyPI result.

## Compatibility and migration

The new VLM API is additive. Existing packed vector, quaternion, and matrix
storage remains unchanged. Rebuild native and Python consumers and discard
pre-1.0 binary, pipeline, execution-plan, and serialized spatial caches.

VLM retains one fixed OA convention: right-handed coordinates, `+Y` up,
camera-forward `-Z`, row-major storage, row-vector composition, Vulkan depth
`[0, 1]`, and top-origin raster mapping. External formats convert once at their
import/export boundary rather than patching VLM matrices.

## Known limitations

- Performance qualification currently covers one Intel/Clang Linux host;
  compiler and cross-platform matrices remain open.
- Checked inverse, affine, normal-matrix, and per-point unprojection operations
  intentionally perform more validation than their raw GLM peers.
- VLM is CPU-only. Batch-array SIMD remains with `oa::FnSimd`, and GPU-resident
  spatial work requires a measured consumer.

## Upgrade

Update to `v0.7.28`, rebuild native and Python consumers, and regenerate
pre-1.0 caches. Code that manually writes camera, projection, affine, normal,
or viewport matrices should migrate to the corresponding named `oa::vlm`
operation.
